epistemic_policy: Every discovered record remains CANDIDATE_UNREVIEWED until human review.
Model-generated synthesis, classifications, embeddings, inferred entities and reasoning chains are not evidence.
Similarity does not imply historical descent, common origin or diffusion.
Publication, version, index, release/update and discovery dates remain distinct.
Archaeological observations remain distinct from inferred symbolic, ritual, social or cognitive meaning.
Ancient-DNA affinity, IBD sharing, culture, language, political identity and social identity are not interchangeable variables.

priority_queue_delta_vs_2026_09_15.note: Indexing/ranking movement only; not an evidence-state change.

new_candidates.title: Population genomics, demography, and circum-Baltic connectivity of Early Medieval southwestern Finland
new_candidates.candidate_relevance: Genome Biology reports 34 analysed ancient individuals from Late Iron Age/Early Medieval southwestern Finland, circum-Baltic IBD links, inland continuity, and a later coastal ancestry shift interpreted in relation to Swedish immigration.
new_candidates.epistemic_caution: Genetic affinity, IBD networks and ancestry shifts do not by themselves establish ethnicity, language, political identity or cultural identity. The timing and cause of migration are model- and source-supported interpretations, not direct observations.

new_candidates.title: Large estimated size of the Australian Indigenous population before its extensive decline following colonial invasion
new_candidates.candidate_relevance: Nature Human Behaviour integrates ethnographic observations, archaeological and genetic reconstructions and carrying-capacity models, reporting a bootstrapped median pre-colonial population estimate of 2.22 million and severe post-invasion demographic decline.
new_candidates.epistemic_caution: The pre-colonial population is a model-derived continental estimate, not a census. It must not be projected to individual communities or used to overwrite community histories; genetic effective population size and carrying capacity are not direct headcounts.

new_candidates.title: Hydroclimate complexity across the last glacial cycle in tropical Australia: reassessing the uniqueness of the Holocene
new_candidates.candidate_relevance: The study synthesizes 69 palaeoenvironmental archives spanning about 130,000 years and argues that declining temporal resolution with age can make Holocene hydroclimate appear uniquely heterogeneous.
new_candidates.epistemic_caution: Proxy-resolution and archive-density differences can masquerade as environmental complexity. Climate proxies must not be converted into causal claims about human behaviour without matched chronology, exposure and alternative-model tests.

new_candidates.title: Middle voice markers in the languages of the world
new_candidates.candidate_relevance: Zenodo v1.0 provides a CLDF StructureDataset of middle-voice markers intended for comparative linguistic analysis.
new_candidates.epistemic_caution: Typological resemblance or shared grammatical structure does not establish common ancestry, historical descent, migration or cultural identity. Language-family and contact controls remain necessary.

new_candidates.title: New technology illuminating ancient evidence: Re-evaluating Meretneith's serekhs and political position
new_candidates.candidate_relevance: A Prague Egyptological Studies article digitally re-examines the sole surviving photograph of a lost mud-stopper inscription and argues that two disputed serekhs contain signs consistent with Meretneith's name, supporting a revised political-role hypothesis.
new_candidates.epistemic_caution: Digital enhancement of a scan of an archival photograph is derived evidence, not an independent physical observation. The original artifact and glass plate are unavailable; identification and reconstructed career stages require expert source review.

provenance.provider: Prague Egyptological Studies via author-authored public report

new_candidates.title: Phytoliths from Cloggs Cave, GunaiKurnai country (southeastern Australia) reveal the gathering of whole grasses for burning practices inside the cave
new_candidates.candidate_relevance: Burnt phytoliths and whole-grass indicators provide evidence of people transporting and burning plants inside Cloggs Cave over a long stratigraphic sequence; the study was conducted with GunaiKurnai Land and Waters Aboriginal Corporation.
new_candidates.epistemic_caution: Burnt phytoliths support human plant-burning activity, not automatic proof of an unchanged ritual meaning across 25,000 years. Unburnt phytoliths can include non-human contributions; Indigenous knowledge and permissions must not be stripped from context.

new_candidates.title: Sant'Elpidio a Mare Picene burial with ceramic grave assemblage
new_candidates.candidate_relevance: Italian heritage-authority reporting identifies part of a composite ceramic grave assemblage near Sant'Elpidio a Mare, provisionally attributed to Picene culture and preliminarily dated to the 6th century BCE; finds were secured for restoration and study.
new_candidates.epistemic_caution: Both cultural attribution and date are explicitly preliminary. Grave assemblage does not by itself establish belief, ritual intent beyond deposition, social rank, identity or a broader regional mortuary norm.
